q: What does the h in ph, th, kh and tsh tell you?
o: A puff of air comes after the consonant
Say it like English f or the th of think
why: In Tâi-lô the h after p, t, k or ts marks a puff of air, like the p of pin.

q: How many syllables does 食飯 (tsia̍h-pn̄g) have?
why: Every character is one syllable; the hyphen joins the two syllables of one word.

q: How is the j in jua̍h (熱, hot) said?
o: A voiced sound, written [dʑ] in phonetic notation
why: Tâi-lô j is a voiced consonant; Bite-size Taiwanese writes it [dʑ].

q: How do you say the nn in sann (三, three)?
o: The vowel goes through the nose, with no n at the end
why: nn marks a nasal vowel: air goes through the nose, and the tongue never closes for an n.

q: 好 hó means good. What is hóo (虎)?
o: A different word: tiger, with the open oo of law
why: o and oo are different vowels, so hó and hóo are different words.

q: How do you end tsa̍p (十, ten)?
o: Close the lips and stop, with no pop
Release the p with a puff
Add a short vowel after the p
why: Final -p -t -k are never released: close and stop.

q: Which tone has the circumflex (â)?
why: The circumflex marks tone 5, the rising tone: kâu (猴, monkey).

q: How does tone 2 sound, as in hóo (虎, tiger)?
why: Tone 2 is a high fall (51), not a rise.

q: pih (鱉) has no mark and ends in -h. Which tone is it?
why: An unmarked syllable ending in -p -t -k -h is tone 4.

q: In a two-syllable word, which syllable keeps the tone you see?
why: Every syllable but the last changes to its sandhi tone; the last keeps its citation tone.

q: In 菜單 (tshài-tuann, menu), tshài has tone 3. Which tone is it said in?
why: In sandhi, tone 3 becomes tone 2.

q: You type 火車 (train) in Tâi-lô. Which tone do you write on the first syllable?
why: Tâi-lô always shows the citation tone, so you write hué with tone 2, even though sandhi makes it tone 1.

q: What does -- before a syllable mean?
o: The two syllables are one word
The syllable after it is said light, in the neutral tone
why: -- marks the neutral tone: the next syllable is light and short.

q: In 失禮 (sit-lé), sit is tone 4 and ends in -t. What happens to it in sandhi?
o: It becomes tone 8: high and low swap
why: Checked syllables in -p -t -k swap in sandhi: tone 4 becomes tone 8.

q: In 多謝你 (To-siā--lí), what happens to siā?
o: It keeps its citation tone, because the light syllable follows
why: The syllable before -- keeps its citation tone.

q: Your friend's grandmother asks you 你食飽未？ What is she doing?
why: 你食飽未？ is an everyday greeting, not an invitation.

q: You broke something at a friend's house. Which of these is an apology?
why: 失禮 is an apology (MOE synonym: 抱歉); 歹勢 would also do. 多謝 is thanks, 再會 goodbye, 𠢕早 good morning.

q: How do you say goodbye?
why: 再會 means goodbye, literally meet again.

q: Which sentence is written in Taigi characters?
why: Taigi writes not as 毋: 我毋是學生.

q: How do you say two books?
why: A number needs a classifier, 本 for books, and two is 兩: 兩本冊.

q: Where does 佇厝裡 (at home) go in 我佇厝裡食飯 (I eat at home)?
o: After the verb, as in English
why: Place with 佇 goes before the verb.

q: How do you ask the teacher to say it again?
why: 請 first, then 閣 (again) + 講 (say) + 一擺 (one time).

q: How do you address Teacher Lîm?
why: The surname comes before the title: 林老師.

q: The teacher is too fast. Which is the course's phrase for 'Speak slowly, please'?
why: 慢慢仔 (slowly, an MOE adverb) + 講 (speak). 說 is Mandarin, and 慢慢仔 is one word that cannot be split.

q: How do you say She's very pretty?
why: No 是 before an adjective: 伊真媠.

q: You invite a friend: Let's go to the night market. Which we do you use?
why: 咱 includes the listener; 阮 leaves them out.

q: How do you say I'm not a teacher?
why: The negative of 是 is 毋是.

q: How do you ask someone's name?
why: The question word stays where the answer goes: 你號做啥物名？, answered 我號做…

q: How do you say 'My surname is Lîm'?
why: 姓 is the verb, so no 是 is needed: 我姓林。

q: In 'I study in Taipei', where does the course put 佇臺北?
o: Twice, before and after 讀冊
why: With an action verb, 佇 and the place come before the verb, as in the MOE's examples: 我佇臺北讀冊。

q: How do you ask 'What do you want to eat?'
why: The question word stays where the answer goes: 你欲食炒飯 → 你欲食啥物？

q: Where does 當時 (when) go in 'When are you coming?'
o: After 你 and before the verb
why: A time word, and the question word for time, goes before the verb: 你當時欲來？

q: A friend says 我欲食炒飯. How do you ask back 'And you?'
why: 咧 after the person sends the question back: 你咧？

q: How do you say 'two people'?
why: Before a classifier, two is 兩: 兩个人.

q: How is 九 read in a phone number?
why: Phone numbers use the literary digits: 空九 is khòng-kiú, while 九 alone, counting, is káu.

q: What is 十二?
why: Read it as it is written: ten, two = twelve. Twenty would be two, ten.

q: How do you say 'mom' in Taigi?
why: Mom is 阿母. 阿媽 is grandma, and 媽媽 is Mandarin.

q: What does 恁小弟咧？ mean?
why: 恁 (you all) works as 'your' with family words, and 咧 sends the question over: and your little brother?

q: Which is a younger brother?
why: 小弟 is a younger brother; 阿兄 is an older one, 後生 a son.

q: How do you say 'I don't have any money'?
why: The negative of 有 is 無: 我無錢。

q: How do you turn 你有冊 into a yes/no question with a particle?
o: Raise your voice at the end
why: 無 at the end, said in the neutral tone, makes a yes/no question: 你有冊無？

q: Where does 敢 go in 'Is this yours?'
o: After the subject 這, before 是
why: 敢 goes after the subject, right before the verb: 這敢是你的？

q: How do you say 'this book'?
why: 這 + classifier + noun: 這本冊. Books take 本.

q: Which classifier goes with 狗 (dog)?
why: Most animals take 隻: 一隻狗.

q: Why does 這 have a different reading in 這敢是你的？ than in 這本冊?
why: Before a classifier 這 has one reading; standing for 'this thing', as here, it has another.

q: How do you ask 'How much is a bowl of noodles?'
why: Name the thing with its classifier, then ask 偌濟錢: 一碗麵偌濟錢？

q: How do you say 'This is very expensive'?
why: No 是 before an adjective: 真 (very) goes in front of 貴.

q: What does 傷鹹 mean?
why: 傷 before an adjective means too: 傷鹹, too salty.

q: How do you say 'I want to drink tea'?
why: 欲 goes before the verb: 我欲啉茶. 要 and 喝 are Mandarin.

q: What does 欲落雨矣 mean?
why: With the weather, 欲 means about to, and 矣 shows the change: it's about to rain.

q: How do you say 'I don't want to eat meat'?
why: The negative of 愛 is 無愛: 我無愛食肉.

q: How do you say 'She's at home'?
why: 佇 alone means is at: 伊佇厝裡. 在 is Mandarin.

q: How do you say 'under the chair'?
why: The place word comes after the noun: 椅仔下跤.

q: How do you say 'I eat at home'?
why: Place with 佇 goes before the verb: 我佇厝裡食飯.

q: Which word means the left side?
why: 倒 is left and 爿 is side: 倒爿. 正爿 is the right side.

q: What does 就到矣 add at the end of 直直行就到矣？
why: 到 means arrive, and 矣 says the change has happened: and then you're there.

q: How do you say 'Turn right at the intersection'?
why: The place, 路口, comes first, then the verb 斡 and the side.

q: Which word means 'get off (a bus, train, car)'?
why: 落車 is get off; 上車 is get on.

q: 'I'm going to Tainan by train' =
why: How you travel, 坐火車, comes before the verb 去.

q: What does 咱來去踅夜市 say?
o: They went to the night market.
We (but not you) are at the night market.
Let's go and stroll around the night market.
Come to the night market tomorrow.
why: 咱 includes the listener and 來去 is 'go now': let's go.

q: Which word means 'yesterday'?
why: 昨昏 is yesterday; 今仔日 is today and 明仔載 tomorrow.

q: Where does 明仔載 go in 'He says he'll come again tomorrow'?
o: Before the verb: 伊講明仔載欲閣來。
At the very end: 伊講欲閣來明仔載。
Before 講: 伊明仔載講欲閣來。
why: The time word goes before the verb it belongs to, here 欲閣來.

q: What does 十二點欲食中晝矣！ mean?
why: 十二點 is twelve o'clock and 中晝 is lunch; 欲…矣 says it is about to happen.

q: What do you call the owner of a night-market stall?
why: 頭家 means boss; it is what you call the person running the stall.

q: 'one bowl of noodles' =
why: Noodles by the bowl take the classifier 碗.

q: 'This bowl of noodles is really good' =
why: No 是 before an adjective: 真好食.

q: Which word means 'egg'?
why: 卵 is egg; 兩 (two) sounds exactly the same.

q: 'cheap' =
why: 俗 is cheap; 貴 is expensive, 傷 too and 較 more.

q: How do you ask 'Boss, how much for a catty of bananas?'
why: The food first, then the amount, then 偌濟錢 at the end.

q: 'It's hot today' =
why: No 是 before an adjective: 真熱.

q: In 伊的糖仔比我較濟, which word means 'than'?
why: 比 introduces what you compare with; 較 means more.

q: What does 傷 add in 傷鹹?
why: 傷 + adjective is 'too': too salty.

q: 'I don't know how (to do it)' =
why: The MOE gives 袂曉 as the opposite of 會曉. 不會 is Mandarin, 會曉 is the positive, and 袂使 means not allowed.

q: Which word is for a skill you have learned?
why: 會曉 is know how; 會使 is permission.

q: How does 這條歌你會曉唱袂？ make a question?
o: With 袂 at the end, in the neutral tone
why: 會…袂 at the end asks 'can you or not?'

q: Which negative means 'no need'?
why: 免 is no need; 莫 is don't!

q: 'I didn't eat breakfast' =
why: For something that didn't happen, the negative is 無.

q: 'Don't come!' (telling someone) =
why: 莫 tells someone not to do something.

q: What does 咧 before a verb show?
o: The action is going on now
why: 咧 + verb is an action in progress.

q: 'It's about to rain' =
why: 欲 (about to) + 矣 (a change): 欲落雨矣.

q: 'I've been there' =
why: 有 + verb + 過 at the end: 我有去過.
